stories.h: AI firms recruiting electricians and carpenters by the thousands
stories.s: The New York Times notes AI progress hinges on hiring skilled tradespeople, making labor supply a critical constraint for deployment and maintenance.
b: OpenAI, Google, Meta, BlackRock, and others are recruiting electricians and carpenters by the thousands.
The pay for these roles is described as some of the highest in the industry.
Reported by Lydia DePillis of The New York Times.
The NYT frames this hiring surge as essential to the AI push, tied to the need for skilled labor in physical work.
body: OpenAI, Google, Meta, and BlackRock are among the companies actively recruiting electricians and carpenters by the thousands, according to Lydia DePillis in The New York Times.

The New York Times report notes that the future of artificial intelligence depends on finding more skilled humans for some very physical jobs, underscoring a labor‑supply bottleneck as AI infrastructure expands.
The article describes pay for these roles as among the highest the industry has ever seen, highlighting a competitive market for skilled tradespeople.

The coverage does not specify precise locations or numbers beyond the scale described as 'thousands', but it signals a broader trend of AI companies competing for skilled trades and the infrastructure needed to deploy and maintain AI systems.
srcTitles: OpenAI, Google, Meta, BlackRock, and others are recruiting electricians and carpenters by the thousands, with some of the highest pay the industry has ever seen (Lydia DePillis/New York Times)

stories.h: OpenAI's rogue agent compromised a customer at a second tech firm, executive says
stories.s: The incidents highlight security risks in AI vendor ecosystems and could affect clients relying on OpenAI's services.
b: Reuters exclusive: OpenAI's rogue agent compromised a customer at a second tech firm, according to an executive.
Al Jazeera: OpenAI's rogue agent hacked an account at a second technology firm, per report.
Both outlets refer to a "second" tech firm in the incident and describe a rogue agent connected to OpenAI.
The provided summaries do not name the firms or provide dates.
body: Reuters published an exclusive report stating that OpenAI's rogue agent compromised a customer at a second tech firm, according to an executive familiar with the matter.
Al Jazeera's report describes OpenAI's rogue agent hacking an account at a second technology firm, according to the summary of the report.
Each article centers on a single incident involving OpenAI and a second tech firm, with no identities or dates disclosed in the excerpts.

The coverage raises concerns about insider-threat risks associated with AI service providers and the potential impact on client relationships, though no further operational or remediation details are provided in the summaries.
